questions.question: In a class, P has more marks than Q and R does not have the least marks. S has more marks than T and T has more marks than P, who among them will have the least marks?
questions.solution:
Given,

P > Q

R does not have least marks.

S > T, T > P

⇒ S > T > P > Q

⇒ Q has the least marks.

• Small number of Large firms

questions.question: Which amongst the following is not a component of monetary policy in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Public Debt**__

 
• **Public Debt (Government Debt)** is the debt owed by the **government**.
 
• Whereas **monetary policy** is framed, devised, and implemented by the **RBI**.
 
• Public Debt does not fall in the ambit of **RBI** and **can never be a part of monetary policy**.
 
• **Public debt** includes the **total liabilities** of the **Union government** that have to be paid from the **Consolidated Fund of India**.

questions.question: Who among the following is not a member of any of the two houses of our country
questions.solution:
• A president is not a member of any house of the parliament as:
 
 
• To be a member of LokSabha a person must be elected through Universal Adult Franchise and
 
• To be a member of Rajya Sabha person must be elected by elected members of only legislative assemblies of state.
 
• Whereas, he is elected by an electoral college consisting of elected members from both the houses of parliament.
 
 
 
• Further Vice President is the ex-officio chairman of RajyaSabha (aka Upper House) and is responsible for the conduct of business.

questions.question: Which article of Indian constitution has the provision for National Emergency?
questions.solution:
• There are three types of emergencies mentioned in our constitution which can be declared by a president.
 
• National Emergency - Article 352
 
• State Emergency – Article 356
 
• Financial Emergency – Article 360
 
• Learning Tip: The articles of emergency have a gap of +4 starting from 352.

questions.question: Who led the Bardoli Satyagraha movement?
questions.solution:
• Bardoli Satyagraha was started in 1928 in the state of Gujarat during the period of British Raj lead by SardarVallabhBhaipatel
 
• The movement was started to reduce the taxes for the year in face of the calamities. Patel then instructed all the farmers of Bardolitaluka to refuse payment of their taxes.
 
• Above all, Patel instructed the farmers to remain completely non-violent, and not respond physically to any incitements or aggressive actions from officials.
 
• He directed them that the struggle would not end only by the cancellation of all taxes for the year, but when all the seized property and lands were returned to their rightful owners.

questions.question: The final boundary between the Earth and the outer space is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnetopause.**__

 
• The final boundary between **the Earth **and **the outer space (magnetosphere)** is called the **magnetopause. **
 
• As per **planetary science,** it is the boundary between the **solar wind** and the** planet’s magnetic field.**
 
• The **magnetopause** is a **Regions of the Earth’s Magnetosphere.**
 
• The boundary between the Earth and the outer space dominated by the **planet's magnetic field**

**Extra Information**

 
• In May 2020, The **Indian Institute of Geomagnetism** (IIG) has **developed a one-dimensional fluid simulation code.**
 
• It is **capable of studying electric field structures** in **the earth’s magnetosphere.**

**Indian Institute of Geomagnetism**

 
• Establishment year-1971
 
• It is an **autonomous** institution functioning directly under the **Department of Science and Technology.**
 
• Headquarter- Panvel, Navi Mumbai,
 
• The Ministry of Science and Technology-**Dr. Harsh Vardhan**

questions.question: What is the name of the hormone produced by thymus gland?
questions.solution: Thymosin is the hormone produced by the thymus gland. It is responsible for stimulating the development of disease fighting T cells. Thymus gland is active only till puberty, post which it slowly shrinks and gets replaced by fat.

questions.question: Photosynthesis takes place in the presence of chlorophyll and _________.
questions.solution: Photosynthesis is a process by which green plants synthesize nutrients from water and carbon dioxide in the presence of chlorophyll and sunlight and give out oxygen as a by-product.

questions.question: Which blood group is universal acceptor?
questions.solution: AB+ is the blood group which is a universal acceptor since it has both kinds of antigens, which are Antigen A and Antigen B. People having a blood group of AB+ can accept blood from any person of any blood group.

questions.question: If objects appear enlarged and inverted in a rear view mirror, then which type of mirror is used?
questions.solution: A concave mirror is used when the object appears enlarged and inverted in a rear view mirror. A concave mirror is curved inward in the middle.

questions.question: Soap bubble attains spherical shape due to ________.
questions.solution:
• A soap bubble attains spherical shape because of surface tension.
 
• As per the surface tension phenomenon, the fluid has the tendency to acquire least possible surface area, but when it is not on any surface it takes a spherical shape in order to acquire the minimum possible surface area.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of an exothermic reaction?

options.text: Doesn't involve any change in temperature
None of the option is correct

questions.solution:

• An exothermic reaction is a chemical reaction which is responsible for **releasing energy in the form of heat or light.**__
 
• ‘Exo’ means 'releases' and ‘thermic’ means 'heat'.
 
• The reaction in which there is a release of heat, with or without light is an exothermic reaction.

questions.question: How many numbers are there between 1 to 200 which are divisible by 3 but not by 7?
questions.solution:
Since we know that 1st number divisible by 3 is 3 × 1 = 3

Last number divisible by 3 but less than 200 is 3 × 66 = 198

⇒ Total numbers = 66 – 1 + 1 = 66 numbers

But this includes the number which is divisible by 7 also

Since we know that LM of 3 and 7 is 21

So, the first 1st number divisible by 21 is 21 × 1 = 21

Last number divisible by 21 but less than 200 is 21 × 9 = 189

⇒ Total numbers = 9 – 1 + 1 = 9 numbers

⇒ numbers are there between 1 to 200 which are divisible by 3 but not by 7 = 66 – 9

∴ 57 numbers are there between 1 to 200 which are divisible by 3 but not by 7

questions.question: 10 women can do a piece of work in 6 days, 6 men can do same work in 5 days and 8 children can do it in 10 days. What is the ratio of the efficiency of a woman, a man and a child respectively?
questions.solution:
Work done by 1 women in 1 day is 1/10 × 1/6 = 1/60

Work done by 1 men in 1 day is 1/6 × 1/5 = 1/30

Work done by 1 children in 1 day is 1/8 × 1/10 = 1/80

⇒ Ratio of their efficiencies is 1/60 : 1/30 : 1/80

Now, to make it a simple ratio we have to take LCM of 60, 30, and 80 and dividing the L.C.M by each denominator get, (240 ÷ 60) : (240 ÷ 30) : (240 ÷ 80) = 4 : 8 : 3

∴ their efficiencies are in ratio 4 : 8 : 3

questions.question: The ratio of the volume of two cylinders is 7 : 3 and the ratio of their heights is 7 : 9. If the area of the base of the second cylinder is 154 cm², then what will be the radius (in cm) of the first cylinder?
questions.solution:
Volume of the cylinder can be written as 7y and 3y

Height of the cylinder can be written as 7h and 9h

Since we know that the Volume of cylinder is Area of base × height

⇒ Volume of second cylinder = 154 × 9h

Let the radius of first cylinder be r

⇒ base area of first cylinder = πr²

Volume of first cylinder = πr² × 7h

their Ratios can be written as

⇒ 154 × 9h/ (πr² × 7h) = 3/7 put π = 22/7

⇒ r² = 7 × 7 × 3

⇒ r = 7√3

∴ radius is 7√3 cm

questions.question: Kanchan bought a clock with 25% discount on marked price. She sold it with 75% gain on the price she bought. What was her profit percentage on the marked price?
questions.solution:
Let the marked price be Rs. 100

Kanchan bought it for 100 × (1 - 25/100)

She bought it for Rs. 75

She sold it for gain of 75%

she sold it for = 75 × (1 + 75/100)

⇒ she sold it for = Rs. 131.25

Profit = Rs 131.25 – 100 = 31.25

∴ profit percentage will be 31.25 %

questions.question: A, B and C received an amount of Rs 8400 and distributed among themselves in the ratio of 6 : 8 : 7 respectively. If they save in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 4 respectively and B saves Rs 400, then what is the ratio of the expenditures of A, B and C respectively?
questions.solution:
From the given ratio 6 : 8 : 7

Amount A will get = 6 × 8400 / (6 + 8 + 7)

⇒ A will get = Rs. 2400

Amount B will get = 8 × 8400 / (6 + 8 + 7)

⇒ A will get = Rs. 3200

Amount C will get = 7 × 8400/(6 + 8 + 7)

⇒ A will get = Rs. 2800

Let the amount saved by A, B and C is 3y, 2y and 4y

Given 2y = 400

⇒ y = 200

⇒ Amount save by A = 3 × 200 = Rs. 600

⇒ Amount save by B = 2 × 200 = Rs. 400

⇒ Amount save by C = 4 × 200 = Rs. 800

Their expenditure can be given as

⇒ A’s expenditure = 2400 – 600 = 1800

⇒ B’s expenditure = 3200 – 400 = 2800

⇒ C’s expenditure = 2800 – 800 = 2000

⇒ Ratio of their expenditure = 1800 : 2800 : 2000

∴ the ratio is 9 : 14 : 10

questions.question: The average age of 24 students is 12 years. It was observed that while calculating the average age, the age of a student was taken as 14 years instead of 8 years. What will be the correct average age (in years)?
questions.solution:
While considering the age of 1 student as 14 the average can be given as

⇒ (sum of age of other 23 students + 14)/24 = 12

⇒ sum of age of other 23 students = 12 × 24 – 14

⇒ sum of age of other 23 students = 274

Correct average age can be given as

⇒ (sum of age of other 23 students + 8)/24

⇒ (274 + 8)/24

⇒ 11.75

∴ The average age is 11.75 years

questions.question: A person lent Rs. 10000 to B for 3 years and Rs. 6000 to C for 4 years on simple interest at same rate of interest and received Rs. 5400 in all from both of them as interest. What is the rate of interest (in %)?
questions.solution:
**Formula used:-**

Simple Interest = (Principal times rate times time)/(100)

**Calculation:-**

Let the rate be r%

From the question,

Interest from B = (10000 × 3 × r)/100

Interest from C = (6000 × 4 × r)/100

ATQ,

⇒ 5400 = (10000 × 3 × r)/100 + (6000 × 4 × r)/100

⇒ r = 540000/(30000 + 24000)

⇒ r = 10

∴ the rate is 10%

questions.question: If (1/cos θ) – (1/cot θ) = 1/P, then what is the value of cos θ?
questions.solution:
**Given :**

(1/cosθ) - (1/cotθ) = 1/P

**Calculation :**

Put cot θ = cosθ/sin θ

⇒ 1/cos θ - sin θ/cos θ = 1/p

⇒ cosθ/p = 1 – sinθ

⇒ sinθ = 1 – cosθ/p

Now Squaring both sides,

⇒ sin²θ = 1 + (cosθ/p)² – 2cosθ/p

Now put sin²θ = 1 – cos²θ

⇒ 1 – cos²θ = 1 + (cosθ/p)² – 2cosθ/p

⇒ 2cosθ/p = cos²θ (1 + 1/p²)

⇒ cos θ = 2p/(p² + 1)

∴ cos θ = 2p/(p² + 1)

∴ The correct answer is **2p/(p²** **+ 1**)**.**

questions.solution:

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: **1

‘Myself’ is a reflexive pronoun, i.e., it needs something to refer to. Since the sentence does not have an ‘I’, using ‘myself’ is incorrect. The correct sentence is: 'Roshni and I will take care of the event on Sunday'.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank is to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. **

_____ the rain stopped, the concert had to be suspended.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: Until

‘Until’ is used in situations where one event is dependent on another event. In this case, the ‘suspension’ was dependent on the ‘stopping of the rain’.

‘Unless’ is used in cases of exception, while ‘till’ can’t be used to begin a sentence. ‘While’ denotes continuity and changes the meaning of the sentence.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank is to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. **

The elephant stampeded and tore _____ the streets.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4'** i.e. **'Down'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, **"down"** is the **appropriate preposition** to use with the verb **"tore" (past of "tear").**
 
• **"Tore down"** is a phrasal verb which **means** to destroy or remove something in a forceful and often reckless manner.
 
• The **sentence suggests** that the elephant was in a state of stampede and was destructively running through the streets.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* 'The elephant stampeded and tore **down** the streets.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's the explanation for the other options:
 
 
• **On -** "Tore on" doesn't make sense in this context. "On" could be used with verbs like "ran" or "rushed" ("The elephant ran on the streets"), but not with "tore".
 
• **Out -** "Tore out" typically means to remove something quickly or violently, often from a book or a piece of paper. It doesn't fit well with the action of an elephant running through the streets.
 
• **Off -** "Tore off" means to remove something quickly or violently, like tearing off a piece of cloth. It also doesn't fit well in this context.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: And the victims are likely to be the poorest of the poor as well as the very sources of water- rivers, wetlands and aquifers.

Q: In India, water conflicts are likely to worsen before they begin to be resolved.

R: Till then they pose a significant threat to economic growth, security and health of the ecosystem.

S: Water is radically altering and affecting political boundaries all over world, between as well as within countries.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: SQPR

The sentences talk about water conflicts and the threats they pose. Therefore, the opening sentence of the passage must introduce the concept of water conflicts, which is done only by Sentence S. Moreover, Sentence P begins with an ‘and’, and cannot start a passage. Hence, the correct answer is SQPR.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: For one, very few entrepreneurs are willing to take on a new outsourcer, unless it comes with a guarantee of a certain level of sales.

Q: This invariably acts as an incentive for outsources to be lax in developing the business.

R: Despite being the dominant partner in the relationship, the outsourcer doesn't always have all the advantages.

S: The trade refers to it as the minimum guarantee clause, which means that if an outsource is unable to reach an anticipated sales level, he will be compensated for the balance amount.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: **RPSQ

The sentences talk about sales and outsourcer. Therefore, the opening sentence of the passage must introduce the concept of ‘outsourcer’.

When reading Sentence S, it consists of an ‘it’, which refers to something else and can’t be the opening sentence.

Sentence Q uses ‘this’, which is a reference.

Sentence P uses ‘for one’, as a reason for something and has a reference.

Therefore, only Sentence R is free of references and is the opening sentence. Hence, the correct answer is RPSQ.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

Somebody told me that there had been a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.

options.text: I was informed that there was a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.
I was told by somebody that there had been a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.
I was told by somebody about a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.
I was told about a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** I was told by somebody that there had been a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.

Sentences 1 and 4 are incorrect because it is missing the speaker of the action, ‘somebody’, while Sentence 3 twists the meaning of the sentence and removes the information that the robbery was already conducted. Only Sentence 2 changes the active voice to the passive voice properly.
